name: DHT22 / AM2302 Humidity and Temperature Sensor
summary: Humidity and temperature on one wire, in a plastic grille you can read in about ten lines of code. Slow, cheap and everywhere.
notes: The one-wire protocol here is not Dallas 1-Wire. The datasheet says so explicitly: it is a custom timing scheme, so it shares no library, no bus and no device addressing with a DS18B20. You cannot put both on one pin.
There is no addressing at all, so one sensor needs one GPIO. Two sensors means two pins.
Read it no faster than once every two seconds. Faster reads return stale data or fail outright, and the sensor self-heats, which biases the temperature it is reporting.
After power-up, wait a second before talking to it. The datasheet asks for this directly, and a read inside that window is the usual cause of a sensor that works only after a reset.
The manufacturer's own connection diagram uses a 1 kOhm pull-up on the data line, not the 4.7 kOhm that most guides repeat. Either works over a short lead; the lower value is the one the maker drew.
Pin 3 is not connected. The datasheet's pin table lists it struck through, left from a revision where it was a second ground. Leave it alone.

The timing is tight enough that reads fail on a busy processor with interrupts running. That is the sensor's fault, not yours, and it is why most libraries disable interrupts for the duration of a read.

The DHT11 is the same shape and protocol with worse everything: 1 percent humidity resolution against 0.1, and no negative temperatures. The AM2302 is the DHT22 with a cable instead of pins, red to power, black to ground, yellow to data.

circuit.title: Minimum circuit

parts.why: Pull-up on the data line, the value the manufacturer's own connection diagram uses. The line idles high and both ends pull it low to talk.
Supply filtering between VDD and GND, suggested by the datasheet for wave filtering rather than required to function.

circuit.note: That is the whole circuit. Data goes to any GPIO, and the sensor needs a second between power-up and the first read.
